Speech by Minister for Defence Chan Chun Sing at the Tanjong Pagar GRC, Queenstown and Radin Mas SMCs’ 61st National Day Dinner on 15 Aug 2026 at Tanjong Pagar Community Club

15 August 2026 Dear Residents of Tanjong Pagar GRC and Queenstown and Radin Mas SMCs, A very good evening to all of you, and thank you for joining us tonight for our nation’s 61st birthday. In the usual Tanjong Pagar tradition, this is an occasion, a special dinner, where we take time to reflect on our journey as a nation, and also to look ahead and reaffirm our commitment to building a better future for Singapore. For those of you who have come to this dinner regularly over the past few years and during Mr Lee Kuan Yew’s time, you would know that this is the time when we have frank conversations on both our challenges and our opportunities for Singapore. Tonight will be no different. Let me start in our national language, Malay, first. For those of you who may not understand Malay, do not worry. Tonight, I prepared some translations for you on the screen. Malay Selamat petang, dan terima kasih semua kerana bersama-sama hadir di sini. Sedang kita melangkah ke dekad baharu ini, kita boleh berbangga dengan bagaimana masyarakat kita terus berkembang, tahun demi tahun, mengalahkan mana-mana statistik. Sedekad yang lalu, seramai 6 daripada 10 belia Melayu berumur 25 hingga 34 tahun mempunyai kelayakan posmenengah atau lebih tinggi. Hari ini, angka itu adalah 8 daripada 10 orang — sementara bilangan yang memperoleh ijazah universiti telah berganda. Di seluruh masyarakat, penjawatan dalam pekerjaan profesional, pengurusan dan teknikal telah meningkat daripada kira-kira seperempat kepada hampir empat dalam 10 dalam masa sepuluh tahun sahaja. Semua ini tidak berlaku dengan sendirinya. Ia memerlukan usaha keluarga, organisasi seperti MENDAKI yang bekerja secara senyap di sebalik tabir, dan pemerintah yang terus melabur — tahun demi tahun, generasi demi generasi. Pertumbuhan stabil ini paling ketara dalam kalangan para pemimpin yang telah dihasilkan oleh masyarakat kita — pemimpin yang bukan sahaja berkhidmat untuk masyarakat Melayu, bahkan juga seluruh Singapura. Anugerah Hari Kebangsaan tahun ini telah menampilkan ramai daripada masyarakat Melayu, yang telah membanggakan negara. Contohnya – Dr Iskandar Jalil dan Dr Ab Razak bin Chanbasha. Selain mereka, pucuk pimpinan masyarakat kita ternyata merangkumi seluruh bidang seni hinggalah sains, menunjukkan kekuatan dan kepelbagaian para pemimpin Melayu kita. Kekuatan sesebuah masyarakat bukan sahaja diukur oleh pemimpin yang dekat dengannya. Ia diukur oleh pemimpin yang diberikan masyarakat tersebut kepada seluruh negara. Saya amat berbesar hati dengan pertumbuhan masyarakat Melayu dan saya menggalakkannya supaya terus berkembang dan cemerlang. Terima kasih. Now, let me continue in Mandarin. Mandarin 大家晚上好。今天的华语分享只有八个字。我们现在在丹戎巴葛，希望看到 ‘老有所养，老有所为’。 ‘老有所养’是新加坡政府对人民的承诺。不管是建国一代，或者是立国一代，只要国家在我们的有限能力范围之内，我们一定承诺把我们的年长者照顾好。这不只是一个政治领袖的承诺，政治团队的承诺，更重要的是，这也显示了我们东方人的优良传统，就是尊老敬贤。所以在场的每一位年长者，你可以放心。 大家都知道，最近世界局势是挺乱的，生活费也不断地高涨。不过我们可以肯定地和大家分享，只要我们的经济继续不断繁荣成长，我们将会把现有的资源好好地处理，跟大家一起分享，更好地去照顾我们年长者，也更好地照顾有需要的新加坡人。在接下来的日子里，财政部将会继续把我们的财政资源管好。在可能的范围之内，不管是CDC补助券还是其他的帮助方面，我们会继续照顾好我们的年长者，还有我们的弱势群体。所以不管是在公积金方面，或者在其他种种补助计划方面，我们也会继续地做到这一点。‘老有所养’这一点在这八个字里面是相对容易的，因为只要我们同心协力，我们就能把有限的资源管理好。 不过今晚我要着重的是接下来的四个字，‘老有所为’。在选区里走动的时候，很常看到有许多其实没有那么老的人，都来跟我讲说：“我已经老了，我已经老了。每次我听到这句话，我就跟他们说，姜是越老越辣 - 你现在没有超过一百岁，不能说是老。所以不要以为退休了之后就没有用了。反而，退休了之后还是有一段很长的路可以走，还是可以继续为国家和社区做出贡献。我们在丹戎巴葛集选区，在女皇镇也有许多的试点计划帮助我们年长者，不只是照顾好，是更好地利用他们的资源和他们的精力来帮助其他的弱势群体，也帮助其他比他们更老的年长者。所以这是我们希望看到的。 政府会继续把我们的年长者照顾好。不过，我们也希望我们的年长者也能踏出一步，更好地利用你的时间、精力，还有更重要的是你人生的历练，来帮助社会有需要的一群，好不好？所以今天在场的所有年长者，以后你见到我，你不要说你老，你要跟我说：“我是姜，我是越老越辣，我越老，可以做得越多，做得更好。好不好？ English Ladies and Gentlemen, let me now continue in English. The world around us is indeed undergoing profound changes. Tonight, I want to share three sets of challenges of challenges and opportunities that we as fellow Singaporeans must pay attention to. Today, it is not an exaggeration to say that the world is a much more dangerous world relative to our past decades. Yet, today, it is a world that Singapore can emerge stronger, if we continue to get our act together. I will speak about the challenges and opportunities in three domains: our security, our economic livelihoods and our cohesion. Navigating a Changing World First, our security. In my mind, it is quite obvious that big power contestations will intensify. They will increasingly deal with others in a transactional manner from their narrow interests rather than to uphold a global system that they do not feel benefits them adequately or as they wish. Beyond their own geopolitical and economic contestations, we can increasingly expect them to want us to be on their side. Their question – “are you with me or with the other side” – will become increasingly common. As I have shared in previous Tanjong Pagar Dinners, those who are irrelevant will have to choose sides. Those who choose sides will soon become irrelevant. We should be cleared eye that we cannot expect others to deal with us on the basis of sympathy or charity. Instead, we must have real capabilities, and our own value-adding propositions and perspectives for others to take us seriously and want to work with us as a responsible, reliable and trusted partner. And so, the path ahead for us is clearly set out. We have to remain closely connected with the rest of the world, whether they agree with us or not. We must deeply understand how the major and other powers interact with one another. We must understand not just what they do, but more importantly, why they do what they do. Only so can we develop propositions that can make Singapore a desired partner. Now, this requires us to be realistic about our own capabilities and imaginative about what is possible. Let us be honest, we will not be able, nor should we, try to fulfil every demand that others place upon us. But we must be able to offer alternatives that make others want to work with us, especially, or even, when there are things that we do not agree on or we cannot fulfil their desires on us.
